What works, and what to check by eye

Build 1's boundary rule was wrong, and everything measured on top of it was distorted. Rebuilt on the known subfamily consensus with 70 bp flanks, then re-measured end to end. Every number below comes from the new corpus. The browser near the bottom holds the alignments themselves, so the numbers can be checked against what the eye says.

STATEWorking

What is done

The corpus is built and stable: 28 curated Talpidae subfamilies across four genomes, re-extracted from assignment_full.tsv on KIT, aligned with the known subfamily consensus as row 1 and 70 bp of real genomic flank. Around it sit five synthetic negative classes and a 400-set resampling side quest.

Three defects from build 1 are fixed, and all three were mine, not the spec's:

  • The boundary anchor. The element is now delimited by the consensus row's first and last nucleotide — no threshold, no smoothing, nothing that moves when the copies are resampled. Reproducibility went from SD 74.2 to 10.7 bp.
  • Flank length. 300 bp forced MAFFT to align unrelated DNA and smeared a 250 bp element across 1200+ columns. At 70 bp the median alignment is 942 columns rather than 3025.
  • Flank background. Measured on ungapped sequence walking outward from each copy's own edge, it now reads 0.30 — the true value for unrelated DNA. Build 1 read 0.50 because it compared sequences after aligning them.
RESULTSWhich variable catches which failure

Each negative has a feature that catches it

AUC against real families. 1.000 or 0.000 is perfect separation — the direction only says whether the feature runs high or low in that negative. 0.5 is blind.

Real families (POS plus side quest, 428 sets) against each negative class.

Reading across the rows

  • cliff and cons_identity_med — perfect against random loci, AUC 1.000. These are Tier 2: do the copies actually support the consensus, and does similarity fall to background outside it. Random loci score a negative cliff.
  • frac_supported — the contamination detector, AUC 0.996 and 0.998 against 10 % and 30 % dilution. It is the fraction of copies exceeding 55 % identity to the consensus, and contamination appears as copies that simply do not support it.
  • elem_len_cv — perfect against 5′ truncation (AUC 0.000) and near-perfect against random loci. Length heterogeneity, exactly as the spec predicts.
  • res_asymmetry — AUC 0.001 against truncation. In build 1 this separated nothing; it needed exact edges. The spec's ragged-5′-edge LINE signature does work.
  • tsd_frac — now functional. 0.74 of copies in real families carry a detectable target-site duplication, median 9 bp, against 0.04 in truncated sets and 0.07 in random loci. Build 1 called this noise because the edges were only known to window resolution.
Median value per class, so the AUCs above can be read against real magnitudes.
CAVEATSDo not trust these yet

Three numbers that look better than they are

  • rank1_excess is confounded. It separates well on paper — 0.0017 in real families, 0.056 at 30 % contamination, 0.135 in random loci — but it only computes at all after imputing missing windows, and the amount imputed tracks the class directly: 0.26 for real families, 0.55 for random loci. Some of the separation is the imputation, not the biology. The spec's central Tier-3 statistic is still not honestly tested.
  • NEGJITTER is caught by an artifact. Its strongest feature is flank_bp_med (AUC 0.960), which is mechanical — displacing the edges changes how much flank remains. Displacement still does not disturb the biology, which is a real robustness result, but it leaves no genuine boundary-shift negative.
  • NEGSPLICE is still mis-designed. Every chimera splices at the same relative midpoint, so it forms a coherent new family rather than a mosaic. It is now caught by tsd_len_med (AUC 0.956) — but that is the splice destroying the TSD, not mosaicism being detected.
READINESSA screen, not yet a classifier

Honest summary. As a screen separating real families from junk, contamination and truncation, this works now and could be run on new candidates today. As the classifier the spec describes — calibrated probabilities plus a mosaicism verdict — it is roughly half built, and the untested half is the half the spec treats as novel.

The alignments behind the numbers

Eighteen sets, picked to be worth an eye rather than to flatter the method: a typical real family from each genome, one of each negative, and the borderline cases — the real family that scores worst, and the negatives that score most like real families. The consensus is the top row; the element is what lies between its first and last nucleotide, with the flank dimmed on either side.

EDGESValidated

The consensus edge as a guess, not a given

The consensus used for the preliminary search may be mis-trimmed, so the boundary is now searched over offsets around it. At each candidate edge the objective is the step in pairwise identity across it; the best edge maximises that step.

Optimising a statistic and then scoring on it would inflate the negatives too, so the optimised value is deliberately not a discriminating variable. What is used instead is the shape of the landscape: a real family should have a sharp, well-localised optimum, junk a flat one. That prediction held.

Prominence of the optimum — peak minus median over the scan. High = the data have a definite opinion about where the edge is.
Class5′ prominence3′ prominencereading

The truncation row is the useful one: flat at the 5′ end, sharp at the 3′ end. That asymmetry in prominence is a third, independent truncation detector.

Validated against ground truth

The consensus edge is deliberately moved inward by 10, 20 or 40 bp and the search asked to recover it. The 5′ edge comes back within 5 bp in 19 of 20 cases, usually within 1 bp, and returns zero when nothing is wrong. Re-run test_edges.py after any change to the objective.

Two findings about the consensuses themselves

  • The 5′ ends are correct. All 28 curated families put the best 5′ edge within ±1 bp of the consensus. The search confirms the existing boundary rather than moving it. It also settles a reading of the profiles above: the identity bump at −20…−10 in the 5′ flank is the A-rich insertion signature, not the element extending further.
  • The 3′ ends are systematically ~7 bp short. 20 of 28 families want to extend outward, median −7 bp, many at exactly −7 — consistent with poly-A being trimmed during consensus construction while the copies keep it. The 8 that want to trim inward instead are mostly those with the weakest 3′ prominence, i.e. no well-defined edge either way.
Limits. The scan reaches ±60 bp, bounded by the 70 bp flank in the alignment — a consensus wrong by more than that is invisible. Fix by carrying a longer analysis flank that never enters the alignment. The width statistic came out at 6 for every class and is degenerate as computed; prominence carries the information. And the refined edges are not yet fed back into the measurement — that second pass is the next step.

Next, in order

  • Compare the boundary calls against your manual calls on a few families. That is the one step that closes spec §6 step 1, and the calls are now stable enough to be worth comparing.
  • Rebuild the chimera negative with breakpoints that vary per copy, and settle whether the SVD detects mosaicism — using a statistic that does not depend on imputation.
  • Add the natural negatives. LINE candidates already exist at teu/line/ on KIT, plus satellites and processed pseudogenes.
  • Port the nesting check from the repo's own TRF-overlap method rather than the spec's coord_cluster, which the hedgehog log found unreliable.
  • Then fit a model — not before natural negatives exist.
